sections.title: Exercise 1 – Match the words to their correct meanings
sections.instructions: Write the correct vocabulary word next to each definition. The words are in a random sequence.

items.prompt: A strong effect or influence on something.
To give up something or decide not to have it.
A method or way of doing something.
items.hint: It is a method or way of doing something.
items.explanation: A technique is a particular method, such as a way of painting.

items.prompt: To act in a particular way.
A painting made directly onto a wall or ceiling.
To make something return to its original or previous condition.
Very attractive or appealing.
To make someone feel isolated or unwelcome.
A violent or uncontrolled outburst of anger.
To believe something is true without having proof.
The state of being alive or real.
To direct something, such as energy or emotions, towards a particular purpose.
Torn, old-fashioned or in poor condition.
items.hint: It describes clothes that are torn or in poor condition.
items.explanation: Raggedy means torn, worn out or in poor condition.

items.prompt: To give a brief summary of the main points.
items.hint: It is a two-word verb meaning to give a short summary.
items.explanation: To sum up means to give the main points briefly.

items.prompt: Very fierce, violent or aggressive.
Including everyone and making sure nobody is left out.
A set of rules or symbols used to communicate information.
The desire or readiness to do something.
At a minimum; no less than.
For the purpose of achieving a goal.
Extremely expensive, rich or impressive.
items.hint: Think of something very rich and expensive.
items.explanation: Lavish describes something extremely expensive or impressive, like a luxury hotel.

items.prompt: Causing great damage, confusion or destruction.
items.hint: Think of a word for great damage or chaos after a storm.
items.explanation: Havoc means great damage or confusion, for example after a storm.

items.prompt: Continuing to do something despite difficulties.
The period or aftermath following an event, especially a death.
To discover or come across something, especially in a book.
Following customs and beliefs that have existed for a long time.

sections.title: Exercise 2 – Complete the sentences
sections.instructions: Choose the correct word from the word bank in Exercise 1. Use each word only once.

items.prompt: The storm caused complete ___ in the town.
items.hint: Think of a word for great damage or chaos after a storm.
items.explanation: Havoc means great damage or confusion, for example after a storm.

items.prompt: She used a special ___ to create the painting.
items.hint: It is a method or way of doing something.
items.explanation: A technique is a particular method, such as a way of painting.

items.prompt: We need to ___ the main ideas of the presentation.
items.hint: It is a two-word verb meaning to give a short summary.
items.explanation: To sum up means to give the main points briefly.

items.prompt: He was wearing a ___ old jacket.
items.hint: It describes clothes that are torn or in poor condition.
items.explanation: Raggedy means torn, worn out or in poor condition.

items.prompt: The hotel was decorated in a ___ style.
items.hint: Think of something very rich and expensive.
items.explanation: Lavish describes something extremely expensive or impressive, like a luxury hotel.

items.prompt: You should never ___ that everyone agrees with you.
The school aims to create an ___ environment.
The children had a ___ when they were told they couldn't go outside.
She showed great ___ to help the homeless.
The new law had a significant ___ on society.

sections.title: Extra – Choose the correct answer (demo)
sections.passage: Tom was very tired after work, so he decided to forgo the party and go to bed early.

items.prompt: What did Tom decide to do?
items.hint: Look at the word 'forgo' in the text.
items.explanation: To forgo something means to go without it, so Tom skipped the party.

items.prompt: Why?

sections.instructions: Decide if each sentence is true or false.

items.prompt: A fresco is a painting on a wall.
Lavish means very cheap.
items.hint: Is 'lavish' a positive word about money?
